item.title: Soane Fakatava

item.content:encoded:
Tongan chef Soane Fakatava is preparing to showcase a fusion of Tongan and Pacific cuisines at an international culinary event in Auckland this month, aiming to put Tonga on the global food map.

Chef Soane is part of an invited cohort of Pacific-based chefs, who will take part in the upcoming ‘Ocean of Flavours: One Ocean, Many Flavours’ event, at Auckland University of Technology ( AUT ) School of Hospitality and Tourism, 21 -22 September, 2026

Head chef at Nuku’alofa’s Seaview Restaurant, Soane told Matangi Tonga today, that he is looking forward to taking part in the high-energy culinary collaboration.

“It is my goal to put Tonga on the global map and represent my family and people well at this international event,” Fakatava said. His signature dishes will feature a suprise fusion of Tongan flavors. “Food is a universal language, but the ocean gives us our specific voice,” he said.

New Zealand chef Peter Gordon is coordinating the Ocean of Flavours dinner menu, which will highlight ingredients from across the Pacific. The event engages with food writers, influencers, and industry stakeholders and culminates in a dinner for the public on September 22.

Fakatava said the event would allow him to share Tonga’s culture through food.

Claudia Urban, Managing Director of the Seaview Lodge and Restaurant, said Chef Soane is one of only eight chefs selected from the Pacific and will be exclusively representing Tonga. Soane was among chefs from Fiji, New Caledonia, Tonga, Samoa, Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea who received an official invitation from the New Zealand Government to participate in the prestigious event.

Chef Soane, who has more than 30 years’ experience in the culinary industry, said passion, respect for food and the use of fresh local ingredients were central to his approach to cooking.

“I think that the most important thing to remember when you’re cooking is to respect and cherish the food you are creating,” he said.

“I always use ingredients that are nutritious for the body and fresh, especially when it is from the ocean. The ocean has a taste that all Tongans and Pacific people love.”

At the Seaview, his a signature dish:‘Red snapper with vegetables in fresh coconut curry sauce and rice’', is served on the chefs weekly special menu.

Soane, attended ‘Apifo’ou College before pursuing culinary studies at ‘Ahopanilolo Technical College, fulfilling a dream held by his mother, Seletute, for him to become a chef.

He later travelled to Germany, where he worked in several respected kitchens and gained international experience, including working under Michelin-starred chef Johann Lafer at Stromburg Castle.

Back in Tonga, Fakatava has prepared meals for members of the Tongan Royal Family and international VIP s. He now combines his international training with traditional Tongan flavours at Seaview Restaurant and mentors hospitality students and aspiring Pacific chefs.
